lessons.title: The First and Second World Wars
lessons.programRef: GCE O Level History — The world wars and international organisations (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Give the main causes of the First World War
Give the main causes of the Second World War
Outline the effects of the two wars, especially on Africa
reviewNotes: Historian to verify: 1914–1918 and 1939–1945 dates, Sarajevo assassination (1914), Treaty of Versailles (1919), League of Nations (1920), outbreak of WWII (Sept 1939), 1945 atomic bombs, the list of causes in syllabus wording, and neutrality of the effects.

Draft for historian review: only widely accepted facts and approximate dates are used; every date, name and interpretation must be verified by a history teacher before release. Political questions are stated neutrally.

blocks.md: The **First World War** lasted from **1914 to 1918**. Its main causes: a system of **alliances** between European powers, **militarism** (arms races), **imperialism** (rivalry for colonies) and **nationalism**. The immediate cause was the assassination of the Austrian archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo in 1914. The war ended with an armistice in **November 1918** and the **Treaty of Versailles** in 1919.

blocks.caption: The two world wars
blocks.alt: A timeline from 1910 to 1950 with bars for 1914–1918 and 1939–1945.

blocks.title: Effects of the First World War
blocks.md: Millions died; empires fell; map of Europe changed; the League of Nations was created (1920) to keep peace; Germany lost colonies, including Kamerun, which were placed under mandate; many countries faced economic problems. Africans served as soldiers and carriers and the war was fought in parts of Africa.

The **Second World War** lasted from **1939 to 1945**. Causes: dissatisfaction with the Treaty of Versailles, the economic crisis of the 1930s, the rise of aggressive dictatorships (Nazi Germany, Fascist Italy, militarist Japan), the weakness of the League of Nations and the failure of appeasement. The war began in September 1939 when Germany invaded Poland.

blocks.title: Effects of the Second World War
blocks.md: Tens of millions died, including in the Holocaust; cities and economies were destroyed; the **United Nations** was created in 1945; the **atomic bomb** was used in 1945; Europe's old powers weakened and the **Cold War** between the USA and the USSR began. In Africa and Asia the war stimulated demands for independence and led to **decolonisation**, mainly in the 1950s and 1960s.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Do not say the League of Nations succeeded in preventing a second war; it failed.
- The two wars are linked: the unresolved problems of the first helped cause the second.
- 'Decolonisation' means the end of colonial rule; it took place over many years and in different ways in different countries.

blocks.title: Example 1: causes
blocks.statement: Name two long-term causes of the First World War and explain one.
steps: Alliances and militarism were long-term causes.
Alliances split Europe into two camps that were bound to help each other.
A local conflict could therefore spread quickly to the whole continent.
blocks.answer: Alliances and militarism (alliances: any local crisis could draw in all the powers).

blocks.title: Example 2: effects on Cameroon
blocks.statement: Explain one link between the First World War and Cameroon's history.
steps: Its colonies, including Kamerun, were taken from it.
Kamerun was divided between Britain and France and later placed under mandate.
blocks.answer: Germany's defeat ended its rule and Kamerun was divided between Britain and France.

lessons.title: The UN, the OAU and African Union, the Commonwealth and La Francophonie
lessons.programRef: GCE O Level History — The world wars and international organisations (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: State the aims and main organs of the UN
Explain the creation and aims of the OAU and the African Union
Describe the Commonwealth and La Francophonie in outline and Cameroon's place in them
reviewNotes: Historian to verify: UN founding 1945, composition of the Security Council (five permanent members), OAU founded May 1963 at Addis Ababa, AU launched 2002, Cameroon in the Commonwealth (1995) and La Francophonie, UN headquarters in New York and the list of agencies.

Draft for historian review: only widely accepted facts and approximate dates are used; every date, name and interpretation must be verified by a history teacher before release. Political questions are stated neutrally.

blocks.md: The **United Nations (UN)** was founded in **1945** after the Second World War to maintain peace and security, develop friendly relations between nations, promote human rights and encourage cooperation. Its main organs include the **General Assembly** (all members), the **Security Council** (15 members, 5 of them permanent: China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States), the **Secretariat** headed by the Secretary-General, the **International Court of Justice** and the **Economic and Social Council**.

blocks.title: UN agencies
blocks.md: UN agencies work in specific fields: **UNESCO** (education, science and culture), **WHO** (health), **UNICEF** (children), **FAO** (food and agriculture), **ILO** (labour), and others. Cameroon, like many African states, joined the UN soon after independence.

The **Organisation of African Unity (OAU)** was founded in **May 1963** at Addis Ababa by newly independent African states. Its aims: unity and solidarity of African states, defence of sovereignty and territorial integrity, the end of colonialism and apartheid, and cooperation for development. In **2002** the OAU was replaced by the **African Union (AU)**, which aims for greater integration, peace, security and development in Africa.

blocks.title: Commonwealth and Francophonie
blocks.md: The **Commonwealth** is a voluntary association of countries, most of them former territories of the British Empire, that cooperate on trade, education, democracy and development. Cameroon joined in **1995**. **La Francophonie** is an organisation of countries and governments that share the French language and cultural links. Cameroon belongs to both organisations because of its history and its two official languages.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- The UN, OAU/AU, Commonwealth and La Francophonie have different roles and membership; do not mix them.
- The OAU was replaced by the AU; the two are not separate bodies in the same period.
- The Commonwealth is not an empire and its members are equal; membership is voluntary.

blocks.title: Example 1: match the aim
blocks.statement: Which organisation promotes health and which promotes education, science and culture?
steps: WHO is the UN agency for health.
UNESCO covers education, science and culture.
Both are specialised agencies of the UN.

blocks.title: Example 2: explain the change
blocks.statement: Why did Africa replace the OAU with the AU in 2002?
steps: Many African leaders wanted stronger integration and more effective action on peace and development.
The AU has wider aims than the OAU, including economic and security cooperation.
The OAU's aim of ending colonialism had largely been achieved.
blocks.answer: To strengthen integration, peace and development after the OAU's goals of independence were largely achieved.
